Hi Sofia,

Thanks again for yesterday's sync. Before we finalize sizing and the procurement request we need two things from Redwood: a reference map for the proposed private VPC topology (control plane/data plane separation) and a provisioning policy that describes how tenants are created, key material is handled, and what egress rules are applied by default. Can you share a versioned reference map and a short runbook we can hand to our platform ops?

Alex — thanks for the clear list. Attaching a first-pass reference map and a short provisioning playbook (see attachments). A few quick answers inline: 

- Control plane egress: by default the control plane uses a dedicated management egress path to a Redwood-managed telemetry endpoint in the customer's region. We can pin telemetry to a private collector if you need no public egress.
- Inference node placement: we recommend colocating inference nodes in a tenant subnet with an egress proxy (shared NAT/egress gateway) for predictable outbound flows. See diagram.
- Per-tenant egress: we include an example ACL/BGP snippet in the runbook that shows how to tag tenant routes and advertise specific nexthops.

I've attached: 1) sofia_vpc_reference_map_v2.pdf (annotated topology, control vs data annotations) and 2) vpc_provisioning_playbook_v2.xlsx (provisioning checklist + example scripts).

Next steps: would you prefer a short walkthrough (30m) with ops + security to walk through the diagrams? I can do Tue/Thu next week.

— Sofia
Sofia Ivanova
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: sofia_ivanova@redwood.com, network@acme-retail.com
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private VPC reference maps & provisioning question

Adding a couple technical notes that should be in the runbook: 

- Control plane proxies: control plane components talk over mTLS to the customer-managed control plane endpoint. We recommend terminating mTLS at a layer-7 proxy in the control plane subnet to centralize cert validation.
- KV cache & data plane: KV cache shards are local to the inference cluster; no control-plane KV data egresses to customer telemetry. Only anonymized telemetry is sent unless you opt in.
- Failover: include a note that when the primary egress gateway is unhealthy we fallback to a regional standby in the customer's VPC (explicitly documented).

Related: I created JIRA INFRA-1129 to track the proof-of-concept route policy we discussed (link in metadata).

- Jonas
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood
